primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic nephropathy (CKD Stage 3b with overt proteinuria)
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily (titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 5 mg, then 10 mg as tolerated)
medications.duration: Lifelong – titrate to BP <130/80 mmHg, review renal function and potassium after 1‑2 weeks and then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce proteinuria and control blood pressure in CKD stage 3b
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line recommendation for ACE‑I/ARB in CKD with proteinuria or hypertension

medications.duration: Lifelong – review glucose logs after 2 weeks, renal function every 6 months
medications.purpose: Slow CKD progression and reduce albuminuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line SGLT2‑i recommendation (TA775) for eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.duration: Lifelong – lipid profile at 4‑6 weeks, then annually
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line statin recommendation for all CKD patients

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive risk of hypoglycaemia when SGLT2‑i is combined with insulin
interactions_checked.action: Reduce basal and prandial insulin doses by 10‑20% and monitor glucose closely for the first 2 weeks
No dose adjustment required; monitor blood pressure and renal function

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and increase fluid retention; patient has eGFR 38 mL/min/1.73 m²
contraindications.alternative: Use acetaminophen for pain if needed

contraindications.reason: Risk of lactic acidosis; patient eGFR 38 mL/min/1.73 m² (dose reduction required if used)
contraindications.alternative: Not required now; insulin already provides glycaemic control

assumptions_warnings: Serum potassium, liver function tests, full lipid profile, and iron studies are not available – baseline labs will be ordered before initiating ACE‑I, statin, and iron supplementation.
Allergy status to ACE‑I or statins is unknown – will be confirmed at next visit.
Blood pressure target assumes the recorded 114/82 mmHg reflects average readings; home BP monitoring will be advised.
No current antihypertensive other than proposed ramipril; if BP remains above target, a thiazide‑type diuretic may be added later.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily, dapagliflozin 10 mg daily, and atorvastatin 20 mg daily to address proteinuric CKD, slow renal decline, and reduce cardiovascular risk. Adjust insulin dose to mitigate hypoglycaemia risk from dapagliflozin. Obtain baseline labs (K+, LFTs, lipids, iron studies) and monitor renal function, electrolytes, and glucose as per NICE NG203 recommendations. Avoid chronic NSAIDs and ensure patient education on diet, exercise, and medication adherence.
